SHANGHAI, 21 February 1935.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / S. B. REGISTRY. / D _______）
（批：HEADQUARTERS / CENTRAL REGISTRY / No. C 9306 / Date.. 21. 2. 35）

Sir,

I should be much obliged to you if you could find
out the present whereabouts of G.L.Hartman, a Netherlands
subject, whose last known address was 4 Park Lane, room
No.8 which place he appears to have left without having
paid his rent.

He has been in the employ of Mr.P.C.Boon, 19 Kiukiang
Road, for whom he sold goods in commission up to a sum of
$ 113.85, which he has failed to remit and for this reason
I should like to get into touch with him.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,

Consul-General.

The Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai Municipal Council,
SHANGHAI.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Special Branch REPORT

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE C. & S. B. REGISTRY. File No. D 1475 Station 1 Date July 15 - 32 19.32）

Subject (in full) G. L. Hartman.

Made by D.P.S. Fitts. Forwarded by （签名）

With reference to the attached letter dated 29.6.32.
from the Netherlands Consulate-General and the attached
report dated 6.7.32. from Wayside Station, I have to state
that one Gerardus Leonrdus Hartman, a Dutch subject, was
recently deported from Kobe on the grounds that he was not
in possession of a passport, and further that he was with-
out visible means of support.
Hartman, who was formerly in the employ of S. Zimmerman,
Importers and Exporters, 368 Kiangse Road, was discharged
on June 24, 1932, and as he stated that he wished to proceed
to Japan, he was given $50 to go and keep away. He is
said to be extremely erratic in his dealings, working quite
well, even brilliantly, for a while, and then losing his
head, stealing small amounts of money belonging to his em-
ployers.
He applied at the local Netherlands Consulate-General
on June 28, 1932 for a new passport to enable him to reach
Japan, stating that his previous passport issued in Hong-
Kong in July 1930, had been lost. In view of his unsav-
oury reputation (known to the Police), no passport, but a
Certificate of Identity bearing an endorsement to the effect
that Hartman was to receive no financial aid or other
assistance from any Netherlands Consulate Official, was
issued to him.
Hartman was assured by his Consulate that this Certi-
ficate of Identity would act in exactly the same manner
as a passport, but when he reached Kobe on July 2nd., he
was unable to pass the Japanese Customs Authorities with
this Certificate, and was accordingly sent back to Shang-

（印：上海公共租界工部局刑事及特别科登记处。档案号 D 1475 巡捕房 1 日期 32年7月15日 - 32年7月19日）

事由（全称） G. L. Hartman。

由 D.P.S. Fitts 呈报。转呈者 （签名）

关于附呈之荷兰总领事馆32年6月29日来函及附呈之路边巡捕房32年7月6日报告，本人谨此说明，荷兰籍民 Gerardus Leonrdus Hartman 近期因无护照且无可见之生活来源，被从神户驱逐出境。
Hartman 此前受雇于江西路368号进出口商 S. Zimmerman，于1932年6月24日被解雇。因其声称欲前往日本，故给予其50美元令其离开并不得返回。据称其行为极不稳定，工作表现时而良好，甚至出色，但随后便失去理智，窃取雇主少量钱财。
他于1932年6月28日向本地荷兰总领事馆申请新护照以便前往日本，声称其1930年7月在香港签发的上一本护照已遗失。鉴于其不良声誉（警方所知），未向其签发护照，而是签发了一份身份证明书，并注明 Hartman 不得从任何荷兰领事馆官员处获得经济援助或其他协助。
Hartman 得到其领事馆保证，该身份证明书之效力与护照完全相同，但当他于7月2日抵达神户时，凭此证明书无法通过日本海关当局，因此被遣返回上

After messages had passed between the Chinese Pass-
port Examination Bureau and the Netherlands Consulate,
Hartman was allowed to take possession of his baggages,
detained by the Chinese Maritime Customs on July 6 when
he arrived back from Japan, and to go his way.
Under the provisions of an agreement between Japan
and the Netherlands, subjects of the latter country are
permitted to enter Japan, if and when they are in possess-
ion of passports which need not bear a Japanese visa.
It would appear therefore, that Hartman, an undesirable
citizen, will experience great difficulty in leaving Shang-
hai for Japan (or for any other foreign port) until his
Consulate decide to issue him with a passport.
Hartman, who at present is unemployed, is residing at
50 Range Road, a boarding house owned by one Ching Pao Kwei,
to which he (Hartman) removed on July 8, 1932.

Salias
D. P. S.

Officer i/c Special Branch.

在中国护照查验处与荷兰领事馆之间互通消息后，Hartman 获准取回其行李，该行李系其7月6日从日本返回时被中国海关扣留，随后任其离去。
根据日本与荷兰之间的一项协议规定，后者之国民若持有无需日本签证之护照，可获准进入日本。因此看来，Hartman 作为一名不受欢迎之公民，在其领事馆决定向其签发护照之前，将难以离开上海前往日本（或任何其他外国港口）。
Hartman 目前失业，居住在虹口路50号，该处为 Ching Pao Kwei（音译）所有之寄宿公寓，他（Hartman）于1932年7月8日搬入此处。

Salias

REPORT
Wayside Station,
Date 6th July 19 32.

Subject (in full) Arrival of Deportee from Japan

Made by J.D.S. Kobayashi Forwarded by D.I. Thurgood

Sir;
A Netherland subject named G.L. Hartman, age 32, was deported from Kobe by the S/S Shanghai Maru(arrived 3.30 p.m. 6/7/32) escorted by P.S. Abe, of the Kobe Police Force, Special Branch.

Enquiries made by the undersigned it was ascertained that Mr Hartman left Shanghai on 29/6/32 by the S/S Shanghai Maru travelling 3rd class. Upon arrival at Kobe when his passport was called for examination, it was found that he was only in possession of a certificate. The Japanese Authorities were not satisfied with this document and got into communication with the Netherland's Consulate at Kobe who refused to accept responsibility. He was therefore detained on board the S/S Shanghai Maru and deported back to Shanghai.

Upon arrival at Shanghai the Chinese Passport Office detained Hartman's baggage owing to his inability to produce a passport, but was allowed to go to his Consulate.

The attached name card was given to the undersigned by Mr. Hartman.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
M. Kobayashi
J.D.S.

事由（全称） 自日本被驱逐者之抵达

由 J.D.S. Kobayashi 呈报 转呈者 D.I. Thurgood

先生；
一名名为 G.L. Hartman 的荷兰籍民，32岁，由神户警视厅特别科的 Abe 警佐陪同，乘坐“上海丸”轮（于32年7月6日下午3:30抵达）从神户被驱逐出境。

经本人查询，获悉 Hartman 先生于32年6月29日乘坐“上海丸”轮三等舱离开上海。抵达神户后，当要求其出示护照以供查验时，发现其仅持有一份证明书。日本当局对该文件不满意，并与驻神户荷兰领事馆联系，但后者拒绝承担责任。因此，他被扣留在“上海丸”轮上，并被遣返回上海。

抵达上海后，中国护照办事处因 Hartman 无法出示护照而扣留其行李，但允许其前往领事馆。

附上的名片系 Hartman 先生交给本人的。

此致
敬礼，

M. Kobayashi

Date 30 / 6 / 32

SHANGHAI, 29 June 1932 .

Sir,

With reference to your letter of November 8th 1930,
No. S.B.D. 1475, I venture to enquire whether the Police have
lately received any information as to the present activities
of G. L. Hartman.

He called at my office yesterday stating that he
wished to go to Japan today (June 29th), but that he had
lost his passport, issued to him by the Netherlands Con-
sulate General at Hongkong in July 1930. No new passport
but only a certificate of identity was granted to him.

Thanking you in anticipation of your kind attention
to my enquiry, I have the honour to be, Sir,

Yours obedient servant,

[签名]
Consul,
for Acting Consul-General.

T. P. Givens, Esquire,
Official in charge of Special Branch,
Shanghai Municipal Police,

Sir,

I have the honour to refer to your
letter, No. 3815 of December 1, and to inform you
that G. L. Hartman is now residing at 123 Boone
Road(Room No. 10). He is employed, under the
name of Herman, by Messrs. Zimmerman & Co., 17

of coolies who are engaged in the extermination of
rats by the use of a patent poison, for which the
firm in question acts as agents.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,

Officer i/c Special Branch

REPORT
File No.
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
Special Branch & S. B. Reg. Station,
No. S. B. D. 1073
Date November 19, 1930.
ate 20 - 11 - 30.

Subject (in full) G.L. Hartman.

Made by D.P.S. Moore. Forwarded by D.J. Robertson

Sir,
Ref: attached letter No. 2222 from the Netherlands
Consulate General concerning the above named. The information
relative to his residing at 132 Range Road, is incorrect.
This house is conducted by Cantonese as a dancing school under
the name of the "Narcissus Dance School." Enquiries have
failed to reveal where Hartman is at present living.
He was employed for about eight months during 1928-29
by Messrs Krysmen & Co., Ship chandlers of 19 Minghong Road
as a salesman working on a commission basis. Having previously
served in the U.S. Navy, Hartman was familiar with the
routine and did the majority of his business with the American
naval vessels in port. He performed his duties in a satisfactory
manner until on one occasion after having collected approximately
$300 for goods supplied to the U.S.S. "Pittsburg," he disappeared
and it is believed went to Tientsin.

W. S. Moore
D. P. S.

D. C. (C. & S. Branches)

Filed
O'Fly

先生，
参考：附上的荷兰总领事馆关于上述人员的第2222号信函。
有关其居住在虹口路132号的信息是不正确的。
该房屋由广东人经营，名为“水仙舞校”的舞蹈学校。
经查询，未能查明 Hartman 目前的居住地。
在1928-29年间，他曾受雇于明宏路19号的船舶供应商 Krysmen & Co. 公司约八个月，
担任按佣金制工作的销售员。由于此前曾在美军海军服役，Hartman 熟悉相关例行程序，
其大部分业务是与停泊在港的美国军舰进行的。他一直令人满意地履行职责，直到有一次，
他在为美国军舰“匹兹堡号”（U.S.S. "Pittsburg"）供应货物并收取了约300美元货款后失踪，
据信前往了天津。

W. S. Moore

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. & S. B. REGIST.
No. S. B. D. 1475.
ate 24 - 7 - 30.

SHANGHAI, 24th July 1930.

Sir,

I have the honour to enclose herewith copy of a letter
addressed by the Inspector General of Police at Hongkong on
16th July 1930 under No. 924/1929 to the Netherlands Consul
General at Hongkong.

I may add that the said G.L. Hartman, mentioned therein,
is a most undesirable person, who is alleged to have swindled
in 1929 his former employers Messrs. Krygsman & Co. of 19
Minghong Road for an amount of $ 225.-, and in general is
a beachcomber of the worst kind, who will always endeavour
to live at other people's expense without doing any decent
work. In Yokohama he was a runner for brothels frequented
by foreigners. Whilst in Manilla and Hongkong he pretended
to be insane.

He is in possession of a Netherlands passport issued
at Hongkong, in which a note has been placed that no Nether-
lands Consular official is to give him any financial or other
assistance.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,
[Signature]
Vice-Consul,
in charge of the Consulate-General.

R.C. Aiers, Esquire,
Deputy Commissioner of Police,
Crime & Special Branches,

以第924/1929号发给荷兰驻香港总领事的信函副本。

此外，信中提到的上述 G.L. Hartman 是一个极不受欢迎的人，
据称他于1929年诈骗了其前雇主——明宏路19号的 Krygsman & Co. 公司
225美元，而且总体而言，他是一个最劣质的流浪汉，总是企图不从事正当工作
而靠他人为生。在横滨，他是外国人常去的妓院的跑腿。
在马尼拉和香港期间，他假装精神失常。

他持有一本在香港签发的荷兰护照，其中注明任何荷兰领事官员
不得向他提供财政或其他援助。

S.B. D. 1475.

POLICE HEADQUARTERS
HONGKONG
No.C.I.D. 924/1929.
16th July 1930.

Sir,

G. L. Hartman.

I have the honour to inform you that the abovementioned
person, who was a destitute in the House of Detention, pro-
duced to the Superintendent of the House of Detention on
10.7.30 a letter from the Master of the s.s."Carlier" (Bel-
gian Flag) to the effect that he (Hartman) was being given
employment as a work-away on board the ship as far as
Shanghai. On the strength of this letter, the Superintendent
of the House of Detention released Hartman, who as far as
the Police are aware, duly sailed on the ship.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,
(sd) L.H.V.Booth.
p. Inspector-General of Police.

The Consul-General for The Netherlands,
HONGKONG.

谨通知您，上述人员原是拘留所内的贫困被拘禁者，
于1930年7月10日向拘留所所长出示了一封来自比利时籍轮船“Carlier号”船长的信，
信中称他（Hartman）将在该船上作为抵债劳工工作直至上海。
凭此信件，拘留所所长释放了 Hartman，据警方所知，他已 duly 乘船离境。

谨此致意，
先生，
您顺从的仆人，
(签名) L.H.V.Booth。
